subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw core own a staged multi-agent collaboration architecture covering capability profiles, shared blackboard state, layered memory visibility, and token-cost governance, or should the remaining work be narrowed to plugin/ClawHub/on-ramp RFCs such as teleconference?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses persistent state, memory privacy, config/defaults, delegation authority, and token admission, and repository vision both supports better agent harness capabilities and warns against heavy orchestration layers in core.

options.title: Sponsor a staged core RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require a maintainer-approved staged plan that starts with explicit security, storage, config, and upgrade contracts before code PRs.

options.title: Narrow to on-ramp RFCs
options.body: Move concrete implementation to narrower items like the teleconference RFC and keep this issue only as architecture background, reducing broad core scope.

options.title: Route to plugin/ClawHub
options.body: Close or defer the core request if maintainers decide the collaboration stack should be an external plugin or bundle using existing extension points.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged core RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require a maintainer-approved staged plan that starts with explicit security, storage, config, and upgrade contracts before code PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent ownership signals across the central subagent/session/memory docs paths and has provided scoping guidance on adjacent multi-agent RFCs.
